name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively releasing across multiple stable branches simultaneously. The latest stable release is v0.60.4 (Open Source) / v1.60.4 (Enterprise), released on May 7, 2025 (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases/tag/v0.60.4). A beta release v0.61.0-beta is also available as of May 4, 2025. Multiple older branches (54.x through 59.x) continue to receive patch updates, indicating long-term support across versions. Detailed changelogs per release are linked from each release page on GitHub.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition uses a commercial license.
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases across several branches published on May 7, 2025.
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase Cloud (managed cloud) is available at metabase.com.
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition.
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, MongoDB, Presto, Druid, Oracle, Spark SQL, Vertica, and more via drivers.

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Looker Studio
alternatives.review: Looker Studio is free and easy to use with Google ecosystem data sources, but is closed-source, cloud-only, and less capable for complex multi-source BI compared to Metabase.

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Tableau offers far more advanced visualization and analytics capabilities than Metabase, but is expensive, proprietary, and has no meaningful free tier for production use.
